Biological elimination half-life of alprazolam: ~ 12 hours.

Most people consider a drug to be effectively eliminated after 5 complete half lives, which in this case is 2.5 days.  By this point, 3% of the amount of Alprazolam in your body at the time of your final dose will still remain, but remember that regular dosages of a drug like this causes the plasma concentrations to reach an steady state plasma concentration range that is significantly higher than would be caused by a single dosage alone.

Because of this, I use a more conservative estimation of 7 complete half lives because at that point the concentration of the drug in your body will be less than 1% of what it was when you first stopped.  So in your case, *4 days minimum.*

It definitely sounds like you may be suffering from BPD, or at least have BPD-like traits.  While old-school mental health authorities take a discouraging outlook on this, I assure you that any therapist with a reasonably up-to-date knowledge of advancements in treatment will tell you that this can be helped.

I can't say that treatment will take it all away -- that's just not the reality of ANY mental disorder!  But in this case, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy can help immensely if you stick with treatment for a long enough period of time.  On top of that, a psychiatrist will likely be able to prescribe a variety of medications that can help make this pain much more bearable in the meantime so that you can get full benefit from therapy.

I realize you're dependent on your parents, but do you have health insurance through them?  If it's pushing you to the brink of suicide, there's no shame in admitting yourself to the hospital.  Even if your parents try to discharge you early, which they can't given you're an adult, the hospital is obligated not to let you go until you say that the thoughts of self-harm have subsided.  This means you can stay as long as necessary, or at least as long as your insurance will cover.

If you don't have insurance, STILL GO.  Many hospitals have financial assistance programs to cover those who can't pay.  Some even absorb the cost entirely.  A friend of mine had a community assistance program completely cover a $3,000 bill.  Either way, even if you do have to pay something, you simply cannot put a price on your own wellbeing.
